title: Caching patterns: cache-aside, write-through and write-behind

videos.script: A cache is a copy. The hard part was never making the copy. It is knowing when the copy is wrong. {{copy}} In this lesson you write the pattern most applications use. Ask the cache. On a miss, ask the database, and keep what it said. {{aside}} Then you change a price, and watch the cache keep the old one. {{stale}} You run two writers at once and see why a cache entry is deleted rather than overwritten. And you meet a slow reader that puts the old price back after you deleted it. {{races}} Then the other patterns. Writing through the cache. Writing behind it, and what that risks. {{patterns}} Caching a book that does not exist. And retiring every key at once, with one number. {{keys}} By the end, you can say which pattern a system uses, and what it costs. {{end}}
